title: OCP-IP master: software transactions (single words and INCR bursts of up to 8, posted writes) issued on an OCP master port with SCmdAccept backpressure and a 64-clock accept timeout

regs.name: REQ
regs.desc: Transaction descriptor, then the further data words of a write burst; writing REQ2 commits it

fdesc.req_wdata: write data: the first word with the descriptor, then one word per commit
fdesc.req_posted: 1 = posted write (MCmd WR, no response from the slave); 0 = non-posted write (MCmd WRNP)
fdesc.req_len: burst length 1 to 8 (0 is 1; above 8 is clamped to 8 and sets ERR)

regs.name: RESP
regs.desc: One beat per read data beat, per write completion and per posted write or timeout; reading RESP1 frees it

fdesc.resp_err: 1 = SResp FAIL / ERR, or no SCmdAccept for 64 clocks

irqs.name: ERR
irqs.desc: a burst length above 8, an SResp FAIL / ERR, or an accept timeout; the core holds this until reset, so the bit cannot be cleared before then

notes: MCmd, MAddr, MData, MByteEn, MBurstLength, MBurstSeq, SCmdAccept, SResp, SData and SRespLast are the OCP master pins; they pass through unchanged.
RESP holds one beat: a read burst's beats are kept only when the slave spaces them at least as far apart as software reads RESP; a beat arriving while RESP is full is dropped (RESP_OVF).
